title: The Annual Revision Chamber

features.name: the revision table
features.desc-on-touch: A wide table where honey-records are spread each spring. The same notes, the same corrections, written over and over. The organism has learned that knowing and re-knowing are the same thing.

features.name: the cycle counter
features.desc-on-touch: Marks scratched into wood, one for each year the apiary has revised itself. The scratches form a pattern now — not a line, but a kind of spiral, as if counting itself has become its own dance.

features.name: the spring-returning record
features.desc-on-touch: A file-card that updates itself each season. The same information, refined. The handwriting grows steadier with each revision, as though the organism is learning to be more itself by repeating exactly what it already knows.

features.name: the dance-memory anchor
features.desc-on-touch: An old diagram showing the spring dance in all its annual variations. Each year looks identical. The diagram has learned that true repetition is not failure; it is mastery becoming habit, becoming bone.

features.name: the hive-tongue archive
features.desc-on-touch: Recordings of the hive-song, layer upon layer, each spring's recording played atop the last. The voices are identical. The difference is that each year, the hive knows itself more completely.
